# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the EXACT tasks you broke/fixed) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — teach the prompt the replay+grader mechanics: values not code/formula, derive dynamically
Discovered the governing mechanic (from adapter.py + evaluation.py): the agent's final code is REPLAYED on 2 hidden inputs with different data and graded on recalc'd cell VALUES. Three additive prompt edits, each targeting a real failing cluster:

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; section + cluster):
  - prompt.md new bullet — "make a macro/VBA/formula" = the OPERATION; write resulting DATA VALUES, never VBA/macro source or prose into a cell. Cluster: 157-4, 254-34 (0/3, dumped VBA text).
  - prompt.md rewrote "prefer literals" → firm contract: compute in Python, never leave a `=`-formula as a cell value (unsupported/volatile fn or missing recalc → raw text = 0); conditional-formatting excepted. Cluster: 10281, 32023, 45944, 50526, 50682, 53023, 53062, 55039 (~8, 0/3, formula-as-value).
  - prompt.md new bullet — code re-runs on 2 hidden inputs with different data → derive every value/count/bound/index from the file (ws.max_row / actual extent), never hardcode sample constants. Cluster: 18137, 50755, 577-40.
  - prompt.md pre-finish 3-point checklist operationalizing the above for gpt-5.5.

- Expected effect + why safe:
  - Macro/VBA rule: additive; only 157-4/254-34 write code-as-value (verified by scan), no passing task does → bounded.
  - Literal-vs-formula: biggest lever; touches the whole formula class so I READ every passing formula task first — CF_7349 is conditional formatting (excepted), 45581 already writes a cached value, the rest («redacted») use simple COUNTIF/VLOOKUP/IF/COUNTIFS/SUMPRODUCT that compute literally with near-certainty. Literal is the canonical graded value for every one, so no passing task should flip.
  - Replay/no-hardcode: reinforces the generalization passing tasks already satisfy (they pass all 3 hidden cases).

- Building on prior RESULTS: none (seed iteration).
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet.
- High-value clusters NOT cracked: ~22 per-task logic errors (wrong lookup/grouping/edge-case semantics) — not prose-fixable without overfitting; "current date/month" tasks (34-5, 32023) ambiguous (gold used a fixed unknown date).
- ENV faults handed back (do NOT prompt-patch): 253-22 (grader LibreOffice recalc FAILED, flagged in feedback), 55224 (empty instruction field = data defect).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first step).
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, attack the per-task logic clusters via worked examples for the most common operation families (row-delete-and-shift, matched-lookup, running/grouped aggregates); if rejected, check whether the literal-vs-formula rule regressed a passing formula task and, if so, rescope it (narrow to volatile/unsupported functions only) while keeping the two clearly-bounded edits.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.634 Δ=+0.066 · fixed={253-22, 267-18, 347-49, 399-14, 44264, 47699, 50682, 53023, 55224, 58484} · broke={139-16, 31420, 35747, 42930, 49237, 53957}.
<!-- cand_0001: ACCEPTED val=0.634 Δ=+0.066 -->

## Iteration cand_0002 — three additive generalization rules: read-scope, type fidelity, #N/A lookups
Diagnosed all 25 failing + 15 flaky traces with 5 parallel read-only subagents; separated ~24 per-task logic errors + casing ground-truth noise (skipped) from 3 NEW generalizable clusters iter1 did not cover. All failures are wrong-values (code runs & saves) — no environment fault.

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; section + cluster):
  - prompt.md new bullet after Sheet-Level line — "answer_position bounds WHERE YOU WRITE, not what you READ": read/scan/aggregate over full extent (`ws.max_row`), locate read-columns by HEADER not by offset from the answer range. Cluster: 250-20, 49782 (flaky), 53305, 55039 (0/3), 50526.
  - prompt.md new bullet — value-and-TYPE fidelity: coerce text→number/date before any compare/aggregate/match, normalize string keys, and WRITE numeric answers as numbers (grader type-compares: `"1"`≠`1`). Cluster: 35747, 58890, 53062, 50486, 250-20.
  - prompt.md new bullet — unmatched lookup → write literal `#N/A`, not None/blank. Cluster: 31420.
  - prompt.md checklist 3→4 points operationalizing the above as an unavoidable pre-finish gate for gpt-5.5.

- Expected effect + why safe:
  - Read-scope: BOUNDED additive; all 51 passers already generalize across 3 hidden cases so they read full extent already (reading full extent is a no-op for them); does not loosen the WRITE constraint. Fixes flaky/0-3 tasks that hardcoded `max_row=20`/read-offsets from the answer range.
  - Type fidelity: BOUNDED additive; scoped to compare/aggregate/match + numeric OUTPUT — coercion is a no-op on consistent data, passers already write numbers as numbers; text codes/labels untouched ("intended answer is a numeric quantity/date").
  - #N/A: BOUNDED additive; fires ONLY on an unmatched lookup key — passing lookup tasks find all matches (pass 3/3) so the branch is never taken.

- Building on prior RESULTS: built ON accepted cand_0001. Edits 2 & 3 REPAIR iter1's broke={31420, 35747} (its literal-not-formula rule made the agent compute lookups/counts in Python then mishandle #N/A and text-typed values). These are new orthogonal rules, NOT a re-run of iter1's diff. Did not re-add any iter1 regressing edit.
- Refuted hypotheses: none proven yet; deliberately did NOT add a casing rule (4225 `"Non green"`, 10281 `"Pass"`) — subagent showed GT casing contradicts the instruction & adjacent cells, so a casing rule would be wrong and regress passers.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: ~24 per-task logic/interpretation errors (398-14 sign, 254-34 compute-vs-format, 146-49/413-15 unspecified output order, 32468 EOMONTH window, 18137 count-vs-sum, 32023 layout, 6698 formula semantics, 49237/139-16/42930/53957 one-offs). No safe general prose rule — would need worked examples per operation-family (risk overfit).
- Plateau signal: n/a (2nd step, iter1 accepted). If this rejects, check whether read-scope over-read regressed a Sheet-Level aggregate passer; if so rescope it to "don't hardcode a bound equal to the answer-range extent" only, keep type-fidelity + #N/A.
- Focus next iteration: if accepted, attack the unspecified-output-ORDER cluster (146-49, 413-15) and the compute-vs-format misread (254-34) with a targeted contract line + one worked example each; then the EOMONTH/date-window family.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.641 Δ=+0.007 · fixed={139-16, 18137, 31420, 35747, 53062, 53957, 56561} · broke={430-43, 47699, 58484, 61-4}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0002: rejected val=0.641 Δ=+0.007 -->

## Iteration cand_0003 — salvage cand_0002: keep the 2 safe rules, DROP the type-coercion breaker
Built on champion cand_0001. cand_0002's RESULT (rejected) showed broke={430-43,47699,58484,61-4}. I attributed all 4 to cand_0002's edit #2 (type-fidelity: coerce text→number + write numeric answer as number): those tasks COPY/reproduce cell values (430-43,61-4,58484) or intentionally SKIP non-numerics in an aggregate (47699) — forced coercion/retyping corrupts them. The other two rules never touch them (they already read full-extent + by-header; none is a lookup).

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; section + cluster):
  - prompt.md new bullet after Sheet-Level line — RE-INTRODUCE read-scope (answer_position bounds WHERE YOU WRITE, not what you READ; scan full extent, locate cols by HEADER) + NEW worked clause: for row-DELETION, rows below the deletion (incl. below the answer range) shift UP, so read to ws.max_row, pack survivors, fill the bottom from below-range rows not blanks. Cluster: 18137, 157-4 (0/3), reinforces 34-5/269-44.
  - prompt.md new bullet — RE-INTRODUCE #N/A: unmatched lookup writes literal `#N/A`, not None/blank (unless instruction says leave empty). Cluster: 31420.
  - prompt.md checklist 3→4 points: added full-extent/by-header read check + #N/A-on-miss check. Did NOT add any type/coercion/write-as-number check.
  - DROPPED cand_0002's type-fidelity rule entirely (the proven breaker).

- Expected effect + why safe:
  - Read-scope + deletion clause: BOUNDED/additive. Passing deletion tasks that blank-pad pass only when there's no below-range data or gold wants blanks — rule is then a no-op; a case where fill-from-below differs would be FAILING now. Broke-tasks 430-43/58484/61-4 already comply → no change.
  - #N/A: BOUNDED/additive; fires only on an unmatched key, gated by the "leave empty" exception. Passing lookup tasks match 3/3 so branch never taken.
  - Net: recovers cand_0002's non-breaking fixes (18137,31420,157-4) with ZERO regressions, unlike cand_0002 which paid −4 breaks for its +7.

- Building on prior RESULTS: used cand_0002 RESULT broke/fixed to isolate the breaker (edit #2). Re-introduced ONLY edits #1 (read-scope) and #3 (#N/A) which did not break a task; DROPPED edit #2. Did not re-add anything else from cand_0002's reverted diff.
- Refuted hypotheses: cand_0002 proved a blanket "coerce text→number / write numeric answers as numbers" rule REGRESSES copy/reproduce + selective-skip tasks (430-43,47699,58484,61-4). Never re-test that rule in blanket form. (Also prior: casing rule for 4225/10281 — GT casing contradicts instruction; do not add.)
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: ~22 per-task logic/edge-case errors (30930 between-occurrences boundary, 32975 running max-in-group, 42930 group-rank, 55912 filtered-count, 398-14 balance sign, 254-34 subset-sum-to-target, 146-49/413-15 output order, 39946 revenue-recognition, 48983 index/match transfer). No safe general prose rule — each needs a per-operation worked example (overfit risk); the type-answer subset (35747,53062) is now un-addressable without the refuted coercion rule.
- Plateau signal: 1 accept then 1 reject. Lever switch this iteration = SUBTRACT the regressing rule rather than add more (consolidation), not another guard. If cand_0003 accepts, next lever = ONE worked example for the single most common safe operation-family (e.g. filtered-count 55912/30930) tested for zero passer overlap; if it rejects, the read-scope/#N/A rules themselves are stochastically regressing a passer — rescope read-scope to deletion-only.
- Focus next iteration: pick ONE operation-family with ≥3 failing tasks sharing identical semantics and add a single copyable worked procedure, verifying no passing task shares that family.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.601 Δ=-0.033 · fixed={139-16, 18137, 31420, 42930, 56561} · broke={267-18, 2768, 347-49, 430-43, 45300, 47699, 58484}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0003: rejected val=0.601 Δ=-0.033 -->

## Iteration cand_0004 — ONE safe output-contract clarification (write the value, not just formatting) + plateau handback
Built on champion cand_0001. Diagnosed all 40 failing/flaky traces with 3 parallel read-only subagents (each compared graded code vs ground-truth answer files) + verified the grader mechanic in adapter.py.

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; section + cluster):
  - prompt.md line 8 (conditional-formatting parenthetical) — sharpened: formatting is done IN ADDITION to, never INSTEAD of, writing the graded value; when the instruction says "highlight/color/conditionally format the cells that…" and answer_position is where the qualifying result belongs, still compute and WRITE that value into answer_position. Cluster: 254-34 (0/3, applied fills, never wrote C2's subset-sum).
  - prompt.md line 13 checklist point (1) — made "actually assigns a computed value into each answer cell, not merely recolored/copied cells with the value left unwritten" an explicit pre-finish precondition, with a "leave blank only if the instruction says to" exemption. Same cluster (structural reinforcement).

- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Both touch-points express ONE additive clarification of the EXISTING output contract (never a new global decision rule). Verified against the same-class passing tasks: CF_7349 + CF_12196 ALREADY write `.value` into their answer range AND format → edit is a no-op for them; all other 49 passers already write values into their answer cells; the blank-exemption protects any intentional-blank gold. So no passing task changes behavior. Targets 254-34, where cand_0001's own "formatting is different" exception let the agent do formatting only and never write the graded value.

- Building on prior RESULTS: built ON cand_0001 (unchanged). Used cand_0002/cand_0003 broke-sets to AVOID their refuted levers. Did NOT re-add: read-full-extent/by-header, fill-from-below-on-deletion, `#N/A`-on-unmatched, text→number coercion.

- Refuted hypotheses (proven by prior RESULTS — never re-test): read-scope + `#N/A` + deletion-fill (cand_0003 broke 7 passers); type-coercion (cand_0002 broke copy/skip tasks 430-43,61-4,58484,47699); casing rule for 4225/10281 (GT casing contradicts instruction). NEW this iter: the 31420 "write the quoted VLOOKUP formula" lever is UNSAFE — it threatens passing 53023 (XLOOKUP, fixed *by* cand_0001's literal rule); do not add.

- High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and why unsafe): (a) ~34 task-specific LOGIC errors (wrong lookup/grouping/condition/sign/tie-break/boundary; flaky ones fail hidden cases 2-3 on semantics, NOT extent) — only a per-task worked example fixes each, which overfits + fails the held-out gate. (b) 4 misleading-instruction traps (585-41 commas, 398-14 hyphen-vs-0, 157-4 "F to M", 577-40 dash) — literal instruction contradicts the graded answer, and the contradictions point in OPPOSITE directions, so any encoded rule regresses a sibling.

- ENVIRONMENT fault handed back (do NOT prompt-patch): 34-5 — code byte-matches the answer on all 3 cases; scores 0 only because the grading sandbox's `date.today()` clock falls outside the surviving-date window on a "current month" task. Likely also 32023 ("current department as of today"). HUMAN ACTION: pin the sandbox clock or exclude time-relative tasks.

- Plateau signal: 1 accept then 2 rejects, both rejects from adding behavioral rules that over-applied on gpt-5.5 and regressed passers. The remaining failure set genuinely resists safe general prose (3 independent diagnoses agree). LEVER SWITCH taken: stop ADDING behavioral rules; this iter is a single bounded output-contract clarification of an existing rule. If this rejects as insignificant, the honest conclusion is the prompt has reached its ceiling on this benchmark — remaining gains require per-task worked examples (overfit-risky) or a non-prose capability (tool/verifier), not another prompt rule.

- Focus next iteration: if accepted, the next safe candidate is a SINGLE worked example for ONE operation-family with ≥3 failing tasks sharing IDENTICAL semantics AND zero passing-task overlap (verify overlap first) — the only remaining lever; if rejected, treat the prompt as at ceiling and report that further prompt edits are net-zero.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.612 Δ=-0.022 · fixed={139-16, 254-34, 35747, 42930, 53957} · broke={267-18, 347-49, 430-43, 47699, 58484}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0004: rejected val=0.612 Δ=-0.022 -->

## Iteration cand_0005 — CEILING handback: no edit passes all three tests; champion prompt preserved unchanged
Re-diagnosed THIS iteration's traces from scratch with 3 parallel read-only subagents (fragile passers / always-fail / flaky). Result confirms cand_0004's plateau call with fresh evidence. I made ZERO prompt edits — every candidate lever fails at least one of REAL/SAFE/VERIFIED, and 3 prior iterations prove a speculative edit is negative-EV here.

- Changes I made: NONE. prompt.md is byte-identical to champion cand_0001. (An intentional no-op: the correct representation of "no safe, verifiable, generalizing edit exists.")
- Why no edit: (1) The 25 always-fail + flaky failures are 7/10 + ~6/8 per-task LOGIC errors (distinct wrong sign/grouping/boundary/parse/tie-break/layout) — only per-task worked examples fix them → overfit, held-out gate rejects. (2) The recurring fragile passer set {267-18,347-49,430-43,47699,58484} is regressed by EVERY added behavioral rule: "write-value-on-format" breaks 4 of them (they produce NO scalar — deletion/hiding/URL-prefix, or deliberately-blank cells); read-scope/header breaks 47699 (headerless, FALSE-marker driven); coerce-to-number breaks 267-18 (URL strings). No discriminating condition includes failing 254-34 while excluding these, so no NARROWING rule is constructible. (3) Checklist shortening fixes no failing task (failures are logic not adherence) → fails VERIFIED.
- Building on prior RESULTS: used LEDGER broke-sets to rule out re-trying refuted levers — type-coercion (cand_0002 broke 430-43,61-4,58484,47699), read-scope+#N/A+deletion-fill (cand_0003 broke 7), write-value-on-format (cand_0004 broke 267-18,347-49,430-43,47699,58484). Did not re-add any of them.
- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): all three above, plus casing rule for 4225/10281 (GT contradicts instruction), and "quote the VLOOKUP formula" for 31420 (threatens 53023). NEW confirmation this iter: the 5 fragile passers are structurally hostile to every obvious additive lever AND partly single-trial-noise sensitive — additive prose cannot clear the significance bar.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and why unsafe): per-task logic (398-14 RET−SALE sign, 413-15 transpose layout, 577-40 sentinel-set match, 18137 timestamp window, 39946 revenue proration, 269-44 deletion edge, 30930 run boundary, 50526 lookup tie, 49237 middle-initial slice, 53957 header match) — each fixable only by an overfit example. 254-34 (answer_position vs highlight instruction) — only cand_0004's refuted rule addresses it. 146-49/413-15 output-order — unstated, task-specific.
- ENVIRONMENT fault handed back (HUMAN ACTION): 34-5 (likely 32023) — clock-relative "current month/today"; sandbox clock 2026-08 ≠ authoring date, so the value logic byte-matches yet the date window scores 0. Pin the sandbox clock or exclude time-relative tasks. Not prose-fixable.
- Plateau signal: 1 accept (cand_0001) then 3 rejects, all from adding behavioral prose that over-applied on gpt-5.5 and regressed the same fragile passer set. Three independent fresh diagnoses this iter agree remaining failures resist safe general prose. LEVER CONCLUSION: the prompt is at ceiling; further prose edits are net-zero-or-negative. Remaining gains require a NON-PROSE capability (a deterministic verifier/tool that computes-and-writes, or per-task fixtures) or fixing the environment clock — none available in this edit space.
- Focus next iteration: do NOT re-attempt an additive behavioral prompt rule (4 iterations of evidence). If the edit space is ever widened beyond prompt.md, the highest-value move is a post-hoc verifier that recalculates formulas to values and refuses code-as-value; within prompt-only, treat the champion as final and hand back.

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.612 Δ=-0.022 · fixed={139-16, 35747} · broke={267-18, 430-43, 58484}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0005: rejected val=0.612 Δ=-0.022 -->

## Iteration cand_0006 (parent cand_0001) — INTENT
- **Read the plateau claim (cand_0005 journal) but did not accept it at face value.** That claim
  came from iterations that all added BEHAVIORAL prose (rules the agent knowingly violated) with
  UNBOUNDED activation, which is exactly why they regressed the fragile passers. I looked for the
  opposite kind of edit: a KNOWLEDGE gap the prompt itself creates, fixable with a NARROW rule
  whose activation condition is false on every fragile passer.
- **Found one untried, evidence-backed cluster: "ignored the sheet's own worked example."** Tasks
  39946 (`=$G$8/365*N4` — code used the wrong denominator), 10281 (`I15=IF(...,"PASS","FAIL")` —
  casing drift), 14207 (highlighted example rows define the match) each provide an in-sheet
  demonstration of the exact operation, and the agent substituted an equivalent-looking-but-wrong
  method. Crucially, cand_0001's "don't hardcode sample constants" rule actively PUSHES gpt-5.5
  away from the constants a reference formula legitimately defines — a self-inflicted knowledge
  tension, not stubborn violation. That makes it prose-fixable.
- **Shipped exactly ONE additive, conditionally-scoped bullet** (+ one checklist clause):
  when the worksheet demonstrates the result (reference formula / worked example / example cells),
  reproduce its exact arithmetic, boundaries, rounding, and output text/casing, reading those
  cells at run time so it still generalizes to hidden files. Deliberately kept it to ONE edit:
  4 rejections prove that batching speculative rules onto this dense prompt sinks the whole
  candidate; every other live cluster overlaps a LEDGER-refuted lever (type-coercion, #N/A,
  deletion-fill, write-type) or is per-task logic that only hardcoding could "fix."
- **Bet:** this converts the 3 deterministic 0/3 zeros above without touching the noise-sensitive
  set, giving a net gain that clears the significance margin. If REJECTED with no fragile-passer
  breakage, the plateau claim is confirmed for prompt-only edits and the champion should be treated
  as final. If it breaks a fragile passer, the conditional scoping leaked — narrow the activation
  condition further (never broaden to "copy nearby cells").

> **RESULT (framework, objective):** REJECTED (champion unchanged) · val=0.656 Δ=+0.022 · fixed={139-16, 31420, 35747, 42930, 50755, 53957, 56561} · broke={267-18, 347-49, 58484}. — its WHOLE batch was reverted; re-introduce only the edits that did NOT break a task above, dropping/redesigning the ones that did.
<!-- cand_0006: rejected val=0.656 Δ=+0.022 -->

## Iteration cand_0007 (parent cand_0001) — REDESIGN cand_0006: keep reference-formula fix, DROP the copy-example leak that broke 267-18/58484
Diagnosed cand_0006's breaker + fixed traces with 2 parallel read-only subagents. cand_0006 reached the
highest val ever (0.656, +7 fixed) but was rejected only for breaking {267-18, 347-49, 58484}. The
subagents proved WHY: its rule conflated (1) a reference/existing FORMULA that defines the METHOD
(39946 `=$G$8/365*N4`; 50755's answer cells literally hold `=D2-D4`/`=F1-F3`; 10281 col-I IF) —
reproducing this GENERALIZES — with (2) a pre-filled SAMPLE ANSWER (58484's "Expected Result" column
1,2,1,1; 267-18's worked example string) — copying this OVERFITS and breaks hidden files. Its "read
those cells at run time" made the agent copy #2 → broke 58484 & 267-18. 347-49 has NO in-sheet
formula/example → its break was pure noise (cand_0005 no-op flipped the same set).

- Changes I made (1 line per edit; section + cluster):
  - prompt.md new bullet after the anti-hardcode line — when the answer/reference cells or a demo
    row-column hold an actual FORMULA for the computation, reproduce THAT formula's exact method
    (references, `/365`-type constants, per-row diffs like `=D2-D4` vs `=B2-B3`, boundaries, rounding,
    output text) not a look-alike, then apply any extra instruction step; reading a formula-defined
    constant at run time is spec-reading, not hardcoding. Cluster: 50755, 39946, 10281 (all 0/3).
  - prompt.md 2nd new bullet — a pre-filled "Expected Result"/example-answer column is NOT a spec:
    never copy those displayed values; compute each answer yourself, reading SOURCE cells not the
    example-answer cells. This REMOVES cand_0006's 58484/267-18 breaks and strengthens the anti-hardcode rule.
  - prompt.md checklist 3→4 — added the reproduce-the-formula-not-a-look-alike + never-copy-sample-answers gate.

- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Bullet 1: BOUNDED/additive; activation "answer/reference cells contain a formula" is FALSE on most
    passers (no-op); on the few with a reference formula (267-18) it reinforces the exact evaluation
    they already do. Fixes deterministic 0/3 50755 (literal `=D2-D4` formulas) + 39946 (`/365`) + 10281.
  - Bullet 2: BOUNDED/additive; no-op unless an example-answer column exists; where it does (58484) it
    enforces the correct non-copying behavior → removes cand_0006's break, cannot make a passer wrong.

- Building on prior RESULTS: built directly ON cand_0006's proven +7 lever (LEDGER row 6). Did NOT
  resubmit its bullet verbatim — redesigned it to split formula(method) from answer(copy), which is the
  documented root cause of its −3. Did NOT re-add any LEDGER-refuted lever (type-coercion cand_0002;
  read-scope/#N/A/deletion-fill cand_0003; write-value-on-format cand_0004).

- Refuted hypotheses (never re-test): type-coercion (broke 430-43/61-4/58484/47699); read-scope+#N/A+
  deletion-fill (broke 7); write-value-on-format (broke 267-18/347-49/430-43/47699/58484); casing rule
  for 4225/10281 (GT contradicts instruction); "quote the VLOOKUP formula" 31420 (threatens 53023).
  NEW this iter: cand_0006's UNqualified "treat any worked example as the spec and read it at run time"
  is UNSAFE — it copies sample-answer columns (58484/267-18). Only the FORMULA-defines-method half is safe.

- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: per-task logic (42930 tie-break on hidden files, 398-14 sign,
  146-49/413-15 output order, 577-40 sentinel, 30930 run boundary, 49237/53957 one-offs) — only overfit
  per-task examples fix them. 14207 = unrecoverable red-highlight font signal (capability gap).
- ENV handed back (HUMAN ACTION): 34-5 / 32023 — clock-relative "current month/today"; sandbox clock
  2026-08 ≠ authoring date, value logic byte-matches yet date window scores 0. Not prose-fixable.
- Plateau signal: 1 accept then 5 rejects, but cand_0006 (0.656) shows a REAL lever exists — the
  rejection was a fixable leak, not a ceiling. This iteration removes that leak. If REJECTED with no
  267-18/58484 break, the reference-formula gains themselves are net-insignificant vs noise and the
  prompt is at ceiling; if it breaks 267-18/58484 again, bullet 1's "evaluate the formula" activated on
  them wrongly → scope bullet 1 to answer cells that are EMPTY (formula lives in a reference/demo cell only).
